workflow.title: A small tool with a clear job.
workflow.body: It starts after you build a candidate pool. It does not fetch prices, backtest a strategy, or place orders.
workflow.input.title: Bring your candidates
workflow.input.body: Use a supported JSON or CSV file. Choose a signal date, selection count, and ranking style.
workflow.review.title: Get another perspective
workflow.review.body: DeepSeek handles A-shares. Gemini handles US stocks. The model can only choose from your pool.
workflow.check.title: Check before saving
workflow.check.body: Validate the structure, count, unique symbols, and explanations. Invalid responses are rejected.
workflow.record.title: Keep the record
workflow.record.body: Save the result alongside inputs, the exact prompt, sanitized requests, raw responses, and hashes.
start.title:
Start with a sample.
No key required.
start.body: Install Python 3.10–3.12 and uv, then paste these commands into your terminal.
start.note: The historical A-share sample has one candidate. A dry run checks the input and shows a plan summary. It does not read credentials, call a model, or save a result.

research.description: What our stock-ranking experiments found: model reliability, rule-based returns, turnover, and the limits of daily observations.
research.title: What have we learned so far?
research.intro: The model tests found reliability problems. Rule-based changes reduced some losses, but none of these studies supports live use. Here are the results, including the ones that did not work.

research.stability.title: Does the answer survive a change in input order?
research.stability.question: The same candidate pools were sent five ways: the original order, three shuffled orders, and anonymous stock identities.
research.stability.finding: Only 34 of 100 calls produced a fully usable result. The minimum was 95. A few usable pairs had high overlap, but there were too few to establish reliability.
research.stability.chart: Fully usable results by input setup
research.stability.denominator: 20 calls per setup. The overall pass requirement was 95 of 100, not a separate target for each setup.
research.gate.name: Check
research.gate.dates: Dates with at least 7 shared picks in every shuffle
research.gate.opaque: Mean shared picks after hiding identities
research.gate.first: First-row selection lift (95% interval upper bound)
research.models.title: Did Pro improve on Flash?
research.models.question: Six dates, two models, and three input setups: 36 calls. Both models returned valid stock lists in every call.
research.models.finding: Pro produced more usable explanations, but both models missed the 17-of-18 requirement. On all six original-order dates, both selected exactly the same stocks in the same order as the numeric rule.
research.models.threshold: Required: {count} of {total} per model. Valid stock lists alone do not count as fully usable results.
research.models.notRun: The second stage and the one-month return backtest were not run. “Not run” is not a zero return.
research.models.costNote: Costs are estimates using the July 16, 2026 price schedule, not current prices or an independently verified bill.
research.guarded.title: Did the first rule-based adjustment help?
research.guarded.question: A six-month replay compared the original numeric ranking with a restricted momentum-and-stability adjustment. No AI calls were made in this replay.
research.guarded.finding: The adjustment lost more than the original rule at all three holding periods. Turnover barely changed. It did not qualify for the next stage.
research.returns.title: Total return at the selected holding period
research.returns.note: January 15–July 15, 2026. Signals after close, entry at the next open, modeled one-way cost 20 bps (0.20%). Candidate pools were rebuilt later; this is not a live track record.
research.guarded.corrected: Average daily difference after removing shared cash-only tail days: {value} bps/day. This is a different measure from total return.
research.guarded.quality: 116 of 119 expected dates were usable; June 30–July 2 had no qualified pools. 6,524 price-limit fields were missing and treated as not tradable.
research.numeric.title: Did the revised numeric rule do better?
research.numeric.question: The next rule gave more weight to daily confirmation, stability, liquidity, and trend, with penalties for overheated candidates.
research.numeric.finding: Some losses were smaller, especially over three sessions, but every tested variant still lost money. The rule was designed after seeing earlier results, and execution data was incomplete.
research.numeric.quality: The estimated daily improvements had intervals crossing zero. Missing prices and price-limit data can affect comparisons. This remains a historical research result, not proof of useful live ranking.
research.turnover.title: Can fewer replacements solve high turnover?
research.turnover.question: A separate 107-session replay tested holding portfolios for three or five sessions and limiting each rebalance to two new stocks.
research.turnover.finding: The cap reduced replacements, but about 7.4 of 10 held stocks were no longer in the current candidate pool. Every tested setup still lost money. Old holdings need fresh eligibility checks before testing this again.
research.turnover.chart: Share of names replaced at each rebalance
research.turnover.stale: No longer in the candidate pool
research.turnover.return: Mean total return across schedule offsets
research.turnover.note: January 15–June 29, 2026; 107 sessions; modeled one-way cost 0.20%. This portfolio test uses a different holding schedule from the daily-selection replay above. Returns are not directly comparable. There are no actual orders or fills.
research.turnover.missing: The sample stops before three missing ranking dates, rather than treating those dates as exchange holidays.
research.daily.title: Daily observations: what is actually available?
research.daily.empty: No verified daily series is included in this snapshot. The reviewed material contains an offline rehearsal from July 18, 2026—not a recent live or prospective performance record.
research.daily.explainer: A daily observation records a decision before later outcomes are known. An offline rehearsal checks the workflow using prepared responses. These are kept separate.
research.daily.rehearsal: The bounded selection matched the numeric rule. The veto made the same stock change as a simple rule. No model API was called, no future returns were measured, and the launch binding was incomplete.
research.daily.note: Validated daily rows include failed terminal states. They record run integrity, not profits or out-of-sample qualification; no daily-return chart is fabricated.
research.source.caption: Source document
research.source.explainer: These are reviewed summaries of archived research reports and receipts. The originals and raw provider responses are retained privately. Hashes identify content; they are not independent timestamps.
research.notes.title: Read the experiments in plain language
research.notes.body: Each note starts with the question, what we tried, what happened, and what to do next. Exact identifiers and methods are kept in the technical section.
research.limit: Historical research and workflow observations only. Candidate pools were reconstructed later; these results do not establish strict historical timing, qualified out-of-sample evidence, or readiness for live trading.
